suggestions.title: Extension: open harder — one rep in the tank, not two

apply.to: Extension 150: take set 1 to ~1 RIR until 9,9 lands

rationale.science: Growth comes from sets taken to roughly 1-3 reps in reserve, and on a cut you defend load rather than chase volume (Schoenfeld 2017; Grgic 2021; Robinson 2024).
rationale.data: Two sessions back at 150 since the 155 crater, both logged at 2 RIR, both totalling 15 reps: 6,9 on 7/24 and 8,7 on 7/28. The 9,9 that reopens 155 has not landed.
rationale.relationship: Identical totals in a different shape means the limit is the opener, not your strength - a harder first set converts the same 15 reps into the 9,9 that reopens 155.

suggestions.predict: Next lower day the opener lands 9 and the pair reaches 9,9, reopening 155 within two sessions.

suggestions.title: Leave the calorie band alone - that drift is your step taper

rationale.science: Metabolic adaptation on a moderate cut is real but modest, around 50-100 kcal/day, and fades once weight stabilises - don't over-blame a plateau on metabolism (Nunes 2021).
rationale.data: Steps ran 19.0k / 21.7k / 18.7k across the June blocks and 15.1k / 15.7k / 16.5k the last three weeks. Your own model already carries two maintenance numbers: 2,590 at hard-block steps, 2,470 at Ease-1 steps.
rationale.relationship: The +186 kcal verdict fits one maintenance line across both step regimes at once, so it reads high - that is the planned Ease-1 taper showing up as fake adaptation. Your rate is 1.2 lb/wk and inside the band; nothing needs adding.

suggestions.predict: Holding the band keeps the rate inside 1.0-1.4 lb/wk, and the maintenance fit settles near 2,470 once a clean post-seal fortnight replaces the frozen reads.
